title: Launch Brief (Draft) — Cloud Marketplace Listing Refresh (AWS + GCP)
content:
Doc status: Draft for cross-functional review (PMM/Partnerships/Docs/Security/Eng). Please leave comments inline and flag any claims that require security/legal verification.

====================
1) Summary
====================
We are refreshing Redwood Inference’s AWS and GCP Marketplace presence to support enterprise procurement paths and reduce onboarding friction.

This launch includes:
- Updated AWS + GCP marketplace listings (positioning, copy, screenshots, FAQs)
- New SKUs aligned to Redwood product lines (Hosted / Dedicated / Private + add-ons)
- Marketplace-ready security documentation bundle (SOC 2/ISO-aligned posture; data handling, encryption/KMS, audit logging, retention/residency; shared responsibility)
- Improved onboarding flow (subscription → entitlement → Redwood org provisioning → first API key → first successful request) + metering/billing dimension correctness

Success looks like:
- Marketplace buyers can complete setup without live help
- Enterprise procurement can validate security posture quickly (security packet answers the “top 20” questions)
- Metering dimensions map cleanly to Redwood internal meters (no billing surprises)

Launch owners:
- Exec sponsor (GTM): Jordan Blake
- Program lead: Chris Osei
- Marketing lead: Camila Reyes
- PMM lead (positioning/SKUs): Soojin Lee
- DevEx/Docs lead: Alex Martinez / Elliot Price
- Security/GRC: Naomi Feldman / Dr. Aisha Rahman / Olga Petrov
- Engineering sponsors: Priya Natarajan (platform), Cole Summers (billing), Chloe Martin (console onboarding)

====================
2) Goals & non-goals
====================
Goals
- Replace legacy listings with updated positioning that clearly differentiates:
  - Hosted API: developer-first, usage-based, fastest time-to-value
  - Dedicated: reserved capacity, predictable throughput, isolation, SLA-backed
  - Private: VPC/on-prem options, regulated workloads, customer-managed networking + key management options
- Make it easy for procurement-led teams to buy through AWS/GCP marketplace (and for sales to support private offers)
- Reduce time-to-first-token for marketplace subscribers by tightening the entitlement/provisioning flow and docs
- Provide a marketplace-ready security packet that accelerates security review and reduces questionnaire back-and-forth

Non-goals (for this launch)
- Major changes to core inference runtime performance (we will reference existing benchmarks only if already approved)
- Replatforming internal billing beyond required marketplace dimension mapping
- Broad website rebrand/positioning rewrite (this is specific to marketplace surfaces + linked docs)

====================
3) Target audiences
====================
Primary
- Procurement-led enterprise buyers who must purchase through AWS/GCP marketplace
- Platform teams standardizing inference across products and regions
- Security/compliance reviewers (need audit logs, encryption, retention, shared responsibility clarity)

Secondary
- PLG users who prefer consolidating spend in marketplace
- SEs/AEs needing repeatable procurement + onboarding playbook

====================
4) What’s launching (scope)
====================
A) Listings & marketplace assets
- AWS Marketplace listing refresh
  - Headline, short + long description, feature bullets, “How it works,” FAQs
  - Updated screenshots (Console, usage analytics, audit logs, rollout controls where appropriate)
- GCP Marketplace listing refresh
  - Similar content structure, aligned wording and claims
- Customer-facing marketplace FAQ (procurement + onboarding + support)

B) Packaging / SKU updates
- New SKU catalog aligned to:
  - Hosted (usage-based)
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity / committed spend)
  - Private (license + support tier, plus compliance add-ons where applicable)
- Add-ons
  - Compliance / extended audit log retention / premium support (final names must match the SKU catalog)
- Clear mapping to internal billing meters + marketplace dimensions

C) Security documentation bundle (marketplace-ready)
- Security overview suitable for marketplace review
- Data handling + retention defaults and controls
- Encryption (in transit/at rest), KMS integration notes, key ownership boundaries
- Audit logs: events, retention, export options (SIEM workflows)
- Shared responsibility model: what Redwood handles vs customer configuration responsibilities

D) Onboarding flow + metering reliability
- Console onboarding entrypoint for marketplace subscribers
- Entitlement verification endpoints + improved error states
- Hardening entitlement sync job (retries, idempotency, alerting)
- Telemetry to measure funnel drop-offs

====================
5) Positioning & messaging (approved direction; final copy may vary by marketplace constraints)
====================
Core value proposition
“Developer-first, production-grade LLM inference with predictable performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”

Messaging pillars
1) Production economics you can control
- Clear levers for latency/cost tradeoffs (batching/caching/routing/quantization profiles as applicable)
- Token-level observability to understand spend and performance

2) Reliability & enterprise readiness
- Predictable throughput and isolation via Dedicated
- Private deployment options for regulated environments
- Graceful degradation/fallback options (where supported) to keep apps online

3) Unified experience across environments
- Same API + operational tooling for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private
- Versioning/rollouts and operational controls to reduce regressions

Proof points / claims guardrails (IMPORTANT)
- Only use security and compliance claims that are explicitly approved by Security + Legal.
- Avoid absolute statements (“never,” “guaranteed,” “fully compliant”) unless backed by contractual terms.
- Ensure copy matches the marketplace security packet and public docs.

Example claim language patterns (preferred)
- “Supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (deployment dependent).”
- “Audit logs are available in the Console and can be exported to SIEM tools (plan dependent).”
- “Configurable data retention controls; default retention described in our Marketplace Data Handling & Retention guide.”

====================
6) Customer experience: end-to-end flow (what buyers should be able to do)
====================
Target flow
1) Subscribe in AWS/GCP marketplace
2) Click through to Redwood Console “Marketplace onboarding” entrypoint
3) Redwood verifies entitlement (and shows clear status / retry guidance if propagation delay)
4) Buyer links or creates a Redwood org
5) Buyer creates API key
6) Buyer makes first successful request (quickstart + copy/paste example)
7) Usage appears in Redwood usage analytics; metering maps to marketplace billing dimensions

Known friction points we must explicitly address in docs/UI
- Entitlement propagation delays (show expected timing + “check again” + escalation path)
- Existing Redwood org linking (avoid duplicates)
- Multiple subscriptions per org (edge case support)
- Region/residency questions (direct link to residency/retention notes and support)

====================
7) Metrics & success criteria
====================
Primary success metrics (target for 30 days post-launch)
- Reduce median time-to-first-token for marketplace subscribers (baseline exists; target to be set by Ben Carter after instrumentation)
- Increase subscription → org provisioned conversion rate
- Decrease support tickets categorized as “marketplace provisioning delay” and “billing dimension mismatch”

Secondary
- Improved listing CTR to “How it works” and docs pages
- Reduction in security questionnaire turnaround time (measured via SE/CS notes + time-to-approval)

Instrumentation requirements
- Telemetry events at key funnel steps: entitlement lookup, org linking, API key creation, first success
- Dashboard for entitlement sync job latency/failure rates + alert thresholds

====================
8) Timeline & milestones (draft)
====================
Dates below are placeholders; align with AWS/GCP partner review windows and internal go/no-go.

Phase 1 — Finalize content + packaging (Week 1–2)
- Listing copy finalized (AWS + GCP) with approvals (PMM + Partnerships + Security)
- SKU naming + mapping finalized (billing + finance guardrails)
- Security packet finalized for marketplace submission links

Phase 2 — Engineering hardening + docs publish (Week 2–4)
- Entitlement verification endpoints shipped
- Console onboarding entrypoint shipped
- Entitlement sync job hardening shipped
- Docs site pages published + final URLs set for submission forms

Phase 3 — Marketplace submission + review loop (Week 4–6)
- AWS listing submission
- GCP listing submission
- Partner review feedback addressed (copy adjustments, missing artifacts)

Phase 4 — Launch + enablement (Week 6–8)
- Announce internally
- Update sales/support enablement
- Monitor dashboards + triage process for the first 2 weeks

Dependencies / gating items
- Partner portal review cycle timing
- Finance/legal sign-off for offer terms and discount guardrails
- Security review of all published claims and security packet language

====================
9) Enablement plan (Sales / SE / CS / Support)
====================
Enablement goals
- Teams know when to route a buyer to marketplace vs direct contract
- Teams can troubleshoot onboarding issues quickly
- Teams can answer common procurement + security questions with consistent language

Deliverables
- Internal one-pager: “How to sell via AWS/GCP marketplace” (process, required fields, private offer flow)
- Support macros for:
  - Entitlement not found / propagation delay
  - Org linking confusion / duplicate org prevention
  - Billing dimension questions
- SE talk track + checklist for procurement-led buyers
- Escalation matrix (Support → Eng/Security/Partnerships) + expected response times

Training sessions (proposed)
- 30 min GTM enablement: “What changed + how to position SKUs” (owner: Soojin Lee)
- 30 min support/CS training: “Marketplace onboarding troubleshooting” (owner: Dev Patel + Chloe Martin)
- 30 min security overview: “How to use the security packet in reviews” (owner: Naomi Feldman)

====================
10) Comms plan (internal + external)
====================
Internal comms
Audience: Sales, SE, CS, Support, Marketing, Partnerships, Product/Eng on-call rotations
Channels:
- #announcements post on launch day with:
  - What changed (SKUs, listings, docs)
  - Links to enablement docs + security packet index
  - Escalation contacts + triage process for first 2 weeks
- Enablement email to GTM teams with “top 10 FAQs” + talk tracks
- Office hours for first 2 weeks post-launch (2x/week)

External comms (lightweight; marketplace-first)
- Marketplace listing updates go live (AWS/GCP)
- Docs updates live (marketplace onboarding guides + marketplace security overview)
- Optional: small blog/docs release note (ONLY if PMM wants; keep it procurement-focused, not a broad brand campaign)

Customer/prospect comms
- For active deals requiring marketplace procurement: SEs/AEs send updated links and a short “what changed” note
- Provide security packet link and a direct path to request evidence (gated) if needed

====================
11) Launch readiness checklist (Go/No-Go)
====================
Listings & assets
[ ] AWS listing copy approved by PMM + Partnerships + Security
[ ] GCP listing copy approved by PMM + Partnerships + Security
[ ] Screenshot set approved (correct UI, no sensitive data, meets marketplace formatting)
[ ] FAQ reviewed for claim consistency and support routing

Packaging / billing
[ ] SKU catalog finalized and matches both marketplaces’ naming constraints
[ ] Internal meters ↔ marketplace dimensions mapping validated in staging
[ ] Finance sign-off: revrec + invoicing notes confirmed for marketplace transactions
[ ] Private offer templates validated (if applicable)

Security
[ ] Security packet index page complete, with clear “what’s public vs gated”
[ ] Data retention + residency statements match product behavior and contract language
[ ] Audit log feature descriptions match plan entitlements and retention
[ ] Evidence access process defined (who grants access, SLA, what can be shared)

Onboarding UX + reliability
[ ] Console marketplace entrypoint enabled
[ ] Entitlement verification endpoints deployed and documented
[ ] Entitlement sync job alerts configured; on-call runbook updated
[ ] Edge cases validated: existing org, multi-subscription, entitlement propagation delay

Docs
[ ] Marketplace onboarding guides published (AWS + GCP)
[ ] Troubleshooting page published and linked from Console error states
[ ] Final URLs provided to Partnerships for submission forms

Analytics
[ ] Telemetry events shipping and visible in dashboards
[ ] Baseline vs post-launch tracking plan confirmed

Support readiness
[ ] Support macros ready + escalation matrix distributed
[ ] Known issues list and workaround guidance documented

====================
12) Risks & mitigations
====================
Risk: Marketplace review delays (AWS/GCP)
- Mitigation: Submit early with complete artifact set; maintain review tracker; respond within 24h on partner feedback

Risk: Billing dimension mismatch or confusing invoices
- Mitigation: Validate mapping in staging; run test subscriptions; add proactive FAQ language; create fast escalation path to billing/eng

Risk: Security claims drift between listing and docs
- Mitigation: Single source of truth for approved security language; security review required for any changes; publish versioned security packet

Risk: Provisioning delays lead to drop-offs
- Mitigation: Console error states + retry guidance; entitlement sync job retries + alerting; support macro for quick triage

====================
13) Open questions (as of last edit)
====================
- Final SKU names: confirm any marketplace character/length constraints and consistency across AWS/GCP
- What is the exact “default retention” statement we can publish publicly vs “available on request”?
- Do we want to promote Dedicated and Private equally on both marketplaces, or tailor emphasis (e.g., Dedicated stronger on AWS; Private stronger on GCP for EMEA residency buyers)?
- What is the recommended path when a buyer already has a Redwood org and purchases via marketplace (best UX to avoid duplicates)?

Appendix: Notes
- If we reference SOC 2 / ISO: confirm the exact wording and scope (current period, entity name) with GRC.
- Any SLO/SLA numbers must match contract language and offering tier (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
